page: Microsoft Azure D4plds_v5 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the DPLDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance is equipped with 154 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable, but does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates average performance in CPU-bound tasks, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests scoring 1822.38 and 7232.57 respectively. Memory performance is mixed; while large-block read and write bandwidths are average at 49.0 GB/sec and 30.16 GB/sec, small-block cached read bandwidth is weak at 283.11 GB/sec, and the PassMark memory score is poor at 1071.92. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average throughput, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench scores fall into the weak tier. Database operations on PassMark score in the average range, though Redis SET operations are weak at 5.68 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4plds_v5 utilizes an ARM-based architecture to deliver dedicated CPU resources with a lower memory footprint, offering a budget-conscious option for workloads that do not require high memory density. Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the benchmark profile, this instance is suited for lightweight compute-focused workloads, basic web serving, and development environments optimized for ARM64 architecture, rather than memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D4plds_v5 is an ARM64-based virtual machine from the DPLDSv5 family, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz, alongside 8.0 GB of RAM and 154 GB of local storage. The instance delivers average performance in multi-core CPU benchmarks and large-block memory bandwidth, though it exhibits weaker results in small-block memory access and synthetic Geekbench tests. Lacking GPU acceleration and featuring a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core, this server is designed as a cost-efficient option for lightweight compute tasks, static web serving, and ARM64-native development workloads.
